title: MEDIGREEN
description: An identity for a shared Mediterranean. Handcrafted objects, maritime patterns and clear visual systems bring fisheries, aquaculture, renewable energy and nature conservation into the same conversation.
note: The visual identity draws on Mediterranean craft and the project’s focus on Maritime Spatial Planning. A coordinated system connects project communication, infographics and campaign posters.
images: Many uses, one sea. MEDIGREEN campaign poster.
Mediterranean references and the development of the visual identity.
Applications across printed and digital communication.

title: A sea in numbers
description: Giving marine statistics a tangible form. A series of infographics makes the scale of aquaculture, small-scale fisheries, marine energy and nature protection visible.
note: The figures and their sources remain part of each original graphic. These are a record of the data used in the project, rather than a live statistical dashboard.
images: Small-scale fisheries in the Mediterranean and Black Sea.

title: Communicating the Maritime Green Deal
description: Making the connections between marine planning and the European Green Deal easier to follow. Editorial design and infographics turn policy relationships into a visual companion for practitioners, decision-makers and sustainability communicators.
note: Report by Annija Danenberga and Folco Soffietti, developed within MSP-GREEN. Infographics by Folco Soffietti; photographs by Annija Danenberga. The selection also includes visual summaries of Green Deal components in maritime spatial plans.
images: Communicating the Maritime Green Deal: cover.
Comparing Green Deal policies and maritime spatial plans.
A visual synthesis of opportunities and challenges.
A spread from the communication companion.

title: CROSSGOV
description: A visual account of how science, policy and society connect. Diagrams and illustrated interfaces organise a complex research methodology into relationships, steps and examples that readers can navigate.
note: Selected graphics from the CROSSGOV Science–Policy–Society Interfaces work. The material presents the analytical framework alongside examples from marine policy contexts.
images: The analytical methodology and its main components.
Mapping relationships in the Northern Adriatic.

title: Research, made visible
description: Drawing the relationships behind marine governance. These works use diagrams and maps to give structure to institutional roles, research processes and the many uses of maritime space.
note: A selection from MSP4BIODIVERSITY, REGINA-MSP and MSP Italy. Each graphic keeps the language and structure of its original project.
images: MSP Italy: uses and planning units in the Tyrrhenian maritime area.
MSP4BIODIVERSITY: the proposed virtual centre and its organisation.
REGINA-MSP: the Sardinian regional strategy for Ocean Literacy.

title: Filière Aquacole
description: An interactive visual exploration of the aquaculture sector, from production to distribution and consumption.
note: Explore the stages directly in the interface below. The content is in French.

title: Plastissea
description: An exploration at sea, for children and the adults reading with them. Drawing, language and scientific knowledge come together in an illustrated story about the marine world and plastic.
note: Text, illustrations and graphic design by Folco Soffietti. Created with support from the European Union through POSEIDONE, Interreg VI-A Italy–Slovenia, with CORILA, Università Iuav di Venezia and CNR-Ismar. ISBN 9788889405475.

title: Idee che cambiano il mondo
description: Ideas have stories. This comic work uses sequential drawing to explore how practices and inventions take shape, including the unexpected history of freestyle swimming.
note: Story concept by Massimiano Bucchi. Adaptation by Folco Soffietti. Read the supplied selection below in its original Italian.
images: Idee che cambiano il mondo: opening page.
Sequential drawing and the history of swimming.

title: Thinking on paper
description: Drawing is a way of working things out. Figures, landscapes, visual notes and half-formed stories share these pages, connecting the more structured parts of my practice with observation and play.
note: A selection of sketches and doodles. These drawings also connect the different areas of this portfolio.

title: Learning through sculpture
description: A space to keep learning with my hands. Working with volume, posture and surface gives me another way to look closely, moving between observation, physical materials and digital studies.
note: The selected works include Gandhi (2018, plaster and glasses), Young Athlete / Marco (2022, plaster), Marching Clown (2024, wax and wood) and Resting Diana / Maria (2026, clay and 3D render).

title: A study in clay
description: A figure studied through weight, gesture and balance. These studio photographs record a work in progress and the physical process of building a form.
note: Original photographs from the studio. The support structure remains visible as part of the working process.
